name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Morgan Griffith seeking re-election with large financial advantage
Challenger Joy Powers raised only about $85K with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price Republican win at roughly 97%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Griffith: a heavily Republican district, incumbency, and a fundraising gap of more than 20-to-1, with no polls or expert ratings suggesting vulnerability. Markets agree, pricing a Democratic win at just 2%.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Griffith or a major scandal would be the only realistic path to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Virginia's 9th District is a deeply Republican seat, and incumbent Morgan Griffith is running for re-election with every structural advantage. The district's partisan lean favors Republicans by more than 20 points, and Griffith has built a campaign warchest of nearly $1 million after raising over $1.8 million.

Democratic challenger Joy Powers has raised only about $85,000 and enters the fall with under $15,000 on hand, with no outside spending on either side to change the picture. No public polls or expert ratings target the race, and prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance. The forecast is a Safe Republican hold, with Griffith expected to win by a wide margin.
